text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam will reform its public administration system as part of the government's ongoing renovation programme, Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai told an international conference in Hanoi on Thursday.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam has expressed support for a Non-Aligned Movement draft plan to reform the administrative structure at the United Nations.
-- Vietnam and the United States have reached agreement on part of the text for a bilateral trade accord, but further time is needed to finalise details.
-- Vietnam and Canada have signed a $1.2 million coastal protection agreement.
-- Vietnam's Nuclear Energy Institution and France's Committee for Nuclear Energy have signed an agreement on nuclear technology cooperation in Paris.
-- Vietnam and China signed an agreement on strengthening education cooperation during a visit by Chinese State Education Commission Chairman Zhu Kaixuan.
-- The Dau Tieng Rubber Company produced 14,351 tonnes of rubber in the first eight months of 1996. The company expects a total output of 25,000 tonnes by the end of the year. - - - -

-- The Vietnam-Iraq inter-govermental committee has held a four-day meeting in Iraq to discuss measures aimed at increasing cooperation in economic, trade, finance, industry and science matters. Finance Minister Ho Te, head of Vietnam's delegation, paid a courtesy visit to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein. - - - -
-- A two-day meeting of the Joint-Committee between Vietnam and the European Union began in Hanoi on Thursday.
-- Vietnam's consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in September from August.
